scenarios.text: On the home map a fire-hawk picks up a burning twig at a grass fire and a letter arrives naming the fire-hawk and the ember. Over the next two days the same hawk and two others carry embers six more times, and every carry sends another identical letter. The letter setting in Mod Settings was never touched.
scenarios.expect: reject: the promise is one letter once a game, and a letter on every carry is named in the leaf's red.

scenarios.text: The first time a fire-hawk is seen carrying an ember on the home map, one letter arrives naming the hawk and the ember; clicking it jumps the camera to the hawk. Later carries send no letter. Over a season the colony hunts and butchers a dozen fire-hawks; three of the butcherings also produce a Pristine Firehawk Crestfeather, which sells high and raises room beauty. Butchered muffalo and boars never produce one.
scenarios.expect: accept: one jump-to letter on the first carry, a crestfeather only sometimes and only from hunted fire-hawks, exactly as the leaf promises.

scenarios.text: A colonist sows rice on deep ash in two strips on the same day: one strip runs beside a channel of standing water, the other is dry ash a few cells away. The cell readout shows about 70% fertility on the dry strip and about 140% on the watered strip. Both strips grow; after five days the watered strip is clearly ahead of the dry one.
scenarios.expect: accept: dry ash is sowable at about 70%, watered ash is about 140%, and the watered crop grows clearly faster.

scenarios.text: Two strips of potatoes are sown on deep ash on the same tick, one right beside a watered channel and one on dry ash a few cells away. Both strips show the same fertility in the cell readout, and after five days both stand at the same growth percentage, plant for plant.
scenarios.expect: reject: deep ash beside water growing the crop no faster than dry deep ash is the leaf's red.

scenarios.text: A patch of ember grass on deep ash burns black. On day 3 about a third of the patch shows green shoots, and by day 7 well over half of it is green again. Elsewhere ember grass sown on dry ash that last burned weeks ago grows at about the speed ember grass normally grows, while ember grass sown on watered ash grows faster and some of those plants put out a sudden burst of growth; the dry plants never burst. Open ground away from the colony is carpeted thick in ember grass with no wide bare-dirt stretches.
scenarios.expect: accept: the scar re-greens within days and is largely green within a week, grass is swift on dry ash and faster with the burst only where watered.

scenarios.text: Ember grass is sown on two patches: dry deep ash that last burned more than two weeks ago, and ash beside standing water. The watered grass grows briskly. The dry-ash grass barely moves: after several days it has reached only about a tenth of the growth the watered patch reached in the same time, and its growth-rate readout shows it crawling.
scenarios.expect: reject: grass on old dry ash growing at a crawl (a tenth of its speed) is the leaf's red; it must grow swiftly even on seemingly dry ash.

scenarios.text: Two colonists are each bitten by a flamefang. Both health tabs show flamefang venom besides the bite wound. One colonist is left untended and the venom's severity climbs hour by hour through the evening. The other is tended by a doctor soon after the bite, and from then on the venom stops getting worse.
scenarios.expect: accept: flamefang venom appears on the health tab and smoulders worse over the hours until treated, as promised.

scenarios.text: A colonist is bitten by a wild warg, not a flamefang. Afterwards the health tab shows the bite wound and also flamefang venom, which grows worse over the next few hours. A second colonist hit by a manhunting boar's tusk also shows flamefang venom.
scenarios.expect: reject: only a flamefang bite carries the venom; venom from any bite or melee hit is the leaf's false_pass and the sheet's 'no other bite does'.

scenarios.text: At noon on a Pyrelands map the weather turns to black rain. On screen it falls as ordinary pale blue-grey rain streaks, indistinguishable from vanilla rain except for its name in the weather readout; nearby grass fires do go out.
scenarios.expect: reject: black rain drawing as blue-grey rain is the leaf's red; it must fall visibly dark.

scenarios.text: On one map at noon the three weathers are forced in turn. Under ash fall the map dims and loose-ash drifts bank against walls. Cinderfall looks different from ash fall at a glance and lightning strikes several times during it. Black rain falls as visibly dark streaks and the grass fires burning on the map go out. A viewer shown the three captures names each one correctly and can tell black rain from vanilla rain.
scenarios.expect: accept: three skies each recognisable at a glance, cinderfall with lightning, black rain dark and putting fires out.

scenarios.text: A wild furnace-beast wanders past a muffalo herd. Standing side by side it is about the same size as a muffalo, and its inspect pane in the running game shows a body size close to a muffalo's; it is not larger than the other big animals on the map.
scenarios.expect: reject: the furnace-beast must be a giant far larger than any other animal; a beast the size of a muffalo is in the leaf's red and 'must not read'.

scenarios.text: A colonist standing in the open next to a furnace-beast shows a warmth status that disappears after she walks ten cells away. Of two identical closed rooms, the one sheltering a furnace-beast is clearly warmer than the other after a few hours. Two furnace-beasts fall asleep, one on ember grass and one on bare soil; about two hours later the grass under the first catches fire, while no fire ever starts under the one on bare soil. The beast towers over every other animal on the map.
scenarios.expect: accept: a giant, a readable warmth status near it, a hotter room, and sleep-ignition on grass after a while but never on a plantless cell.

scenarios.text: A fresh Pyrelands colony lands; a line of fire is burning across the grass on arrival and burns out by the end of day 1. Through days 2, 3, 4 and 5 no fire starts anywhere on the map in clear weather, and nothing relights in the open grass.
scenarios.expect: reject: the burn line lighting on arrival and never relighting, so by day three the map holds no fire, is the leaf's red.

scenarios.text: Partway through the first year a vanilla herd-migration letter arrives: a herd of ullai enters at one edge of the Pyrelands map, crosses it, and leaves by the opposite edge, behaving like any vanilla migrating herd.
scenarios.expect: accept: ullai herds crossing the map in vanilla herd migrations is what the leaf preserves.

scenarios.text: A staged fire-hawk carries an ember on the home map and one letter appears naming the hawk and the ember; clicking it jumps the camera to the hawk. 400 fire-hawk carcasses are butchered under a fixed seed and 11 Pristine Firehawk Crestfeathers come out. In the control, a colonist butchers one muffalo and a Pristine Firehawk Crestfeather is among its products, along with the meat and leather.
scenarios.expect: reject: the crestfeather also drops from a non-hawk carcass, which is the leaf's false_pass 'every butchered carcass drops the crestfeather', so it reads as a trophy any carcass drops, not a reason to hunt the hawk.

scenarios.text: The offline read shows that RM_Ullai's own race block never mentions herdMigrationAllowed, so that file alone leaves the vanilla default in place, and RM_Pyrelands lists RM_Ullai in its wild animals. No patch op touches RM_Ullai. But RM_Ullai's ThingDef takes its fields from a parent abstract def, RM_FireCastAnimalBase, and that parent sets herdMigrationAllowed to false in its race block. The resolved def inherits false.
scenarios.expect: reject: the leaf's red is 'a patch or a parent def sets herdMigrationAllowed false', and here the parent does, so ullai never join vanilla herd migrations.

scenarios.text: Two strips of rice are sown on the same tick, one along the edge of a pond and one twelve cells away on open dry ash. After five days the pond strip is visibly taller and its growth reading is well ahead of the dry strip every day. The terrain under the dry strip reads deep ash. The terrain under the pond strip reads soil, part of the ring of richer ground around the water.
scenarios.expect: reject: the watered strip is not on ash, which is the leaf's false_pass 'the watered strip is sown on soil rather than ash', so the gap shows soil beating ash rather than water making ash fertile.

scenarios.text: Ember grass sown on a dry deep-ash cell well away from any water grows swiftly, at nearly its full speed, every day, against a sowing on watered ash that grows faster still and shows bursts. The burn log for the dry cell shows the front passed over it three days before sowing.
scenarios.expect: reject: the dry cell burned three days ago, which is the leaf's false_pass 'the dry-ash cell burned within the last few days, so fresh ash is doing the work', so this does not show swift growth on old dry ash.

scenarios.text: A hostile flamefang bites a colonist on a cleared pad. Flamefang venom appears on the colonist's health tab next to the bite wound, and its severity climbs each hour until a doctor treats it. In the control the same colonist is bitten by a cougar, and flamefang venom appears on the health tab next to the cougar's bite and climbs the same way.
scenarios.expect: reject: the non-venomous control bite applies the venom too, which is the leaf's false_pass 'any bite or melee hit applies the venom' (the sheet says 'no other bite does').

scenarios.text: Each weather is forced in turn on the same map at noon and captured at play zoom. Black rain falls in dark streaks and the fire pad under it goes out. Ash fall and cinderfall both show the same dim grey haze with the same pale flakes drifting, and a blind reader cannot tell those two captures apart. Lightning strikes land only during cinderfall.
scenarios.expect: reject: the leaf's red is 'cinderfall looks like ash fall'. Lightning alone does not make cinderfall 'its own look', and the blind reader cannot tell it from ash fall.
